name: Vercel
description: Next.js natively, static SPAs, and Express, NestJS or FastAPI as Vercel Functions.

specSections.title: Environments & Configuration
specSections.guidance: Per environment (production, preview): the Vercel projects (one per deployed folder), their URLs and the preview URL pattern, every env var with its scope (build-time public vs server-only), the origin model (Next.js same-origin or proxy via rewrites; static SPA cross-origin with API_BASE_URL and CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS), the database (pooled DATABASE_URL, DIRECT_URL) and whether AIDE_RUN_MIGRATIONS is true. Note serverless limits: no background work.

requiredEnv.description: true where the environment has its own database (production; preview when a preview database exists), else false. The build runs the data pack's migrate command only when true (FR-154, D-V4-13). Derived by AIDE.
requiredEnv.when: data != none && data != data-supabase && databaseHost != none && backendHost != deploy-render && backendHost != deploy-railway

checklist.item: Every folder deployed to Vercel has vercel.json with git.deploymentEnabled {"aide/**": false} and no other true rule matching aide/**
A static SPA on Vercel has no /api rewrite to a fixed backend URL (cross-origin only, D-V4-20) and has the SPA fallback where its preset needs it
Migrations run only in the build command gated by AIDE_RUN_MIGRATIONS, using DIRECT_URL, never in request handlers or at cold start
Functions use the pooled DATABASE_URL and hold no in-memory sessions or background work
No tokens, project ids or .vercel/ in the repo (.vercel is git-ignored)
No CI job, script or package script deploys with the Vercel CLI; AIDE triggers every deploy
.env.example lists every variable the app needs, with placeholders only
